use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: Resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation, so that each ballistic missile track reported on the interface represents a single data point.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation, so that each ballistic missile track reported on the interface represents a single data point.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: C2 JU correlates the two eligible ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface, thereby resolving the dual designation and ensuring that the ballistic missile track reported on the interface represents a single data point.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface are present and eligible for correlation, giving C2 JU a dual designation to resolve.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The two eligible tracks have been correlated and the dual designation is resolved; the ballistic missile track reported on the interface represents a single data point.
in_scope_actions: Correlate two eligible ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface
Resolve the dual designation caused by the two tracks
excluded_adjacent_actions: Using PPLI data from J2 messages to reduce surveillance track reporting redundancy
General minimization of dual designation occurrences and duration across all protocols
variant_dimensions: The criteria or correlation tests that determine whether the two tracks are eligible for correlation

claims.content: C2 JU
Two tracks reported to the interface are present and have been recognized by the C2 JU as eligible for correlation.
The two tracks have passed the course, speed, and altitude differential tests and the correlation tests and restrictions required before correlation is executed.
Positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation have been extrapolated to the same time.

The use case is triggered when a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation and initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation, or when a correlation request from another unit requires the C2 JU to perform correlation tests.
The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation and automatically initiates action to resolve the dual designation.
The C2 JU compares the locally derived sensor data for the two tracks (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
The two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once and are deemed a tentative correlation.

Upon the next correlation stimulus, the same two tracks are tested again and pass the second correlation test with no correlation restriction, and the two tracks are processed for dual designation resolution.
The C2 JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message to all other C2 IUs, requesting them to perform a correlation of the two tracks and identifying the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation.
The C2 JU ceases reporting the Dropped TN and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of automatically initiating correlation after recognizing two tracks as eligible, the C2 JU may manually initiate correlation of any two tracks irrespective of the standard correlation test criteria, correlation restrictions, or correlation requirements; manual correlation is not permitted if the two tracks are of a different E/C, one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.

Diverges from Step 4: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the C2 JU alerts the operator to either change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation, or transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.

Diverges from Step 4: Automatic correlation may be allowed despite the ID conflict restriction if either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend.

Diverges from Step 6: Instead of accepting the requested correlation, a receiving C2 JU may respond with a reverse correlation by transmitting the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 6: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, the Dropped TN has an OCC, and RV is set to 3 (manual correlation), the system executes the correlation using the Dropped TN data and the Retained TN track number.

Diverges from Step 6: If the ID/IAD of the Retained TN and the Dropped TN are different and the difference would result in automatic acceptance of the Dropped TN ID/IAD, the Dropped TN ID/IAD, Special Interest Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type are transferred to the Retained TN.
Diverges from Step 6: If the identity of the Retained TN and the Dropped TN are the same, the associated identification data reported for the Retained TN is retained.
Diverges from Step 7: If the C2 JU initiated the J7.2 and a Drop Track message has not yet been received for the Dropped TN, the Dropped TN is retained as a remote track.
Diverges from Step 7: If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it drops the Dropped TN and transmits the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.

missing_aspects: The claim implies this exception applies 'despite' the restriction generally, but the evidence specifically cites exceptions to paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1g(1) (ID difference) and 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a) (engagement status). The rewrite removes the broader implication to strictly match the cited conditions.

claims.content: If the C2 JU attempts to manually correlate two tracks that are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote, the manual correlation shall not be performed.

A ballistic missile track is considered lost when the JU with R2 does not receive any local sensor data since the last transmitted update, or the JU determines that the track is lost by other system criteria.

When a ballistic missile track is reported with the Lost Track Indicator set to value 1, the reporting JU is assumed to have a TQ of 5 less than that being reported; for example, if a JU is reporting 'Lost Track' data with a TQ of 15, a JU holding 'Tracking' data may assume R2 with a TQ of 11.

If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the Track Numbers are different, the C2 JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message with RV set to 1, using the Source TN from the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.

Receiving C2 IUs accept the requested correlation unless prespecified conditions exist that require or allow rejection. In particular, upon receipt of a J7.2 Correlation message, a C2 JU holding OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (if the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled) shall reject the correlation. Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the rejecting JU transmits a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.
If it is determined that more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported, track decorrelation shall occur.

missing_aspects: The source text specifies that 'two tracks shall not be manually correlated' under these conditions; it does not explicitly describe the actor's attempt ('attempts') or the system's active prevention action ('shall not be performed') as a process step, but rather states the prohibition as a rule.

The claim simplifies the example provided in the evidence ('a JU holding "Tracking" data may assume R2 with the reduced TQ'). The evidence specifically provides an illustrative calculation (TQ 15 -> TQ 11) which supports the '5 less' rule, but the claim's phrasing implies a general capability to assume R2 based solely on the reduced TQ, whereas the evidence frames it as a specific scenario/example of how the TQ difference allows assumption of R2.

The claim combines three distinct rules: general acceptance/rejection criteria (EC-EF-019), a specific mandatory rejection condition regarding OCCs/conflicting IDs upon receiving a J7.2 message (EC-EF-015), and the reporting mechanism for rejection (EC-EF-038). While all parts are supported, the claim presents them as a single continuous flow ('In particular...'). The evidence for EC-EF-015 specifically notes this exception applies 'upon receipt of a J7.2 Correlation message', which is correctly included, but the logical connection between the general rule and the specific exception could be clearer to reflect that the specific exception overrides or details the general 'prespecified conditions'.

claims.content: The dual designation is resolved via correlation, and the retained ballistic missile track reported on the interface represents a single data point.
Upon acceptance of the requested correlation, the receiving IUs retain the designated Retained TN and drop the designated Dropped TN.
If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it drops the Dropped TN and transmits the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.

Upon correlation execution, specific data fields from the Dropped TN are transferred to the Retained TN (Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, and Strength if the Dropped TN was a local or common local track); any nonzero Mode I, II, or III IFF/SIF data from the Dropped TN is transferred to the Retained TN if the corresponding Retained TN data is zero.

Identification data is transferred from the Dropped TN to the Retained TN according to ID conflict restrictions: if restricted and the IDs differ, the last Identity reported for the Dropped TN is processed as an Identity Difference Report for the Retained TN; otherwise, specific ID/IAD and platform attributes are transferred.
After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3), the resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
